summary: idnna 0.1.2 setup.py drops and executes remote Linux binary at install time
details: The pypi package `idnna` (a visual near-miss of `idna`) ships a stub module `djangoo` whose only code is a `hello()` print, while its setup.py overrides the install command with a base64-encoded hook. On `pip install idnna` under Linux, the hook is decoded and passed to exec(compile(...)); the decoded payload calls urllib.request.urlretrieve on https://github.com/totti2188/8gp1Q7iZD3h4VW/releases/download/v1.3A/something, writes the opaque binary to /tmp/something, chmods it 0755, and spawns it detached via subprocess.Popen with start_new_session=True. The download host is an unrelated personal GitHub account, the fetched bytes are unpinned and unverified (no hash or signature check), and the base64 wrapping exists only to conceal the network+exec chain inside setup.py. The declared package description (`HTTP client utilities`) and the shipped `djangoo` stub do not correspond to any legitimate functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
